notes: DRAFT for R-STANCE-e. The dojo stance list Jay approved (J1, Oct 25). Descriptions use only what the repo already says: the kata sheets and self-defense.md. How to stand in each stance (feet, weight, hands) is not written anywhere in the repo, so it is a jayQuestion, never a guess. Game benefits are in drafts/planning/R-STANCE-stances-and-kata-rewards.md, not here.

stances.name: Beginner's
stances.description: Plain standing, before you know a stance.
stances.source: Jay (Oct 25, via Manager): Beginner's Stance is plain standing; the kid doesn't know a stance yet.
stances.howToStand: Just stand the way you normally do.
stances.gameLine: Everyone starts here, and your teacher can teach you stances.

stances.name: Ready
stances.source: Jay (Oct 25, via Manager): Ready is the 'open leg stance', feet shoulder-width apart, fists in front of the stomach.
stances.howToStand: Feet shoulder-width apart, fists in front of your stomach.
stances.gameLine: Steady and even, ready for anything.
stances.beltSource: Jay (Oct 25, via Manager): all stances are learned at white belt.

stances.name: Cat
stances.description: A short step back. It shows up in every kata so far.
stances.source: Basic Form 1-2, Keon, David and Goliath: 'short stepping to rear w/RF into cat stance'.
stances.jayQuestion: One short line on how to stand in cat stance, for kids.
stances.gameLine: Quicker Counters and Dash, but softer blocks.
stances.beltSource: Jay (Oct 25, via Manager): all stances are learned at white belt.

stances.name: Front
stances.description: Step forward into it, ready to block and punch.
stances.source: Keon #3 and #9: 'step forward w/LF into front stance'.
stances.jayQuestion: One short line on how to stand in front stance, for kids.
stances.gameLine: Hit harder, but move a little slower.
stances.beltSource: Jay (Oct 25, via Manager): all stances are learned at white belt.

stances.name: Fighting
stances.description: Jump into it to face a weapon, ready to kick.
stances.jayQuestion: One short line on how to stand in fighting stance, for kids. Is it used in any kata?
stances.gameLine: Strong blocks and fast Focus, but a shorter Dash.
stances.beltSource: Jay (Oct 25, via Manager): all stances are learned at white belt.

stances.name: Horse
stances.source: Jay (Oct 25): 'horse stance is rooted stance'. Not in any sheet in the repo.
stances.jayQuestion: One short line on how to stand in horse stance, for kids. Is it in any kata?
stances.gameLine: Stand still to hit harder, but move slower.
stances.beltSource: Jay (Oct 25, via Manager): all stances are learned at white belt.

jayQuestion: Are there other stances taught at the dojo (for example a back stance)?
gameLineNote: R-STANCE-f: player-facing lines for the Fighting Style screen, saying what each stance does in the game (numbers from #290). They are meant for content/abilities/fighting-style.json `lines[gameId]` (the field #293 wires). #293 is still open, so they wait here to avoid a conflict; copy them across once it merges. Ready keeps its current line (#290: the plain stance, all 0).
idMappingNote: APPROVED (Manager, Oct 25). beginners-stance stays the game id for the new Beginner's Stance, with the same 0 numbers and the Beginner's gameLine. Ready gets a new game id, ready-stance, unlocked by white-belt sign-off like the others. #290 gives Ready only 'everything 0', so it plays the same as Beginner's until the Researcher or Jay gives it its own numbers. Closed: Ready stays a stance players can pick in a fight. No existing id is renamed.

signOff.note: Shown when a teacher signs off a stance. {stance} is the stance name, e.g. 'Cat Stance' (same placeholder style as difficulty.json's {name}).
signOff.line: You learned {stance}! Your teacher saw your hard work.
alternatesRecord: {stance} is yours now. Be proud of yourself!
Your teacher signed off on {stance}. Great training!
